properties.statement:
TYPED TOOL PARAMETER NAMES DISAGREE WITH THE NODE PROPERTIES THEY SET, AND ONE SESSION HIT NINE OF THEM. Each cost a failed call, an error and a retry: `add_decision` rejects `status`; `set_decision_status` wants `decision_id` not `id`; `record_change` wants `target_type`/`target_id` not `node_type`/`node_id`, and `name` not `description`; `governed_by` rejects `note` though describe_schema DOCUMENTS note on GOVERNED_BY; `satisfies`/`allocate` take only from_id/to_id; `create_edge` wants `props` not `properties`; `add_epoch` requires `sequence`, undiscoverable until it fails; `add_capability` rejects `capability_type` and `tier` though nodes CARRY both; `propagate_from` wants `seed_ids` not `node_ids`. NOT ONE IS WRONG ON ITS OWN. Together they mean a fluent session still fails roughly ONE CALL IN FOUR, because the mental model 'typed constructors take the node's own property names' is right often enough to keep being used and wrong often enough to keep costing a round trip. || SOURCE: Observed by the dev_storyflow fleet on 2026-08-15, on reflow2 0.31.0 with served == installed verified through /proc/<pid>/exe. Three agent seats, one shared graph, one day.

═══ A TENTH, FROM A THIRD INDEPENDENT SOURCE, THE SAME DAY (2026-08-15) ═══

`add_component` takes a parameter named `description` and the Component node requires `purpose`. `capture.rs:687` passes `&req.description` straight into the `purpose` slot, so the two names are the same field. `create_nodes` with `node_type: \"Component\"` refuses `description` — `Validation error on Component.purpose: required property is missing` — and because that call is all-or-nothing it failed a SIX-NODE BATCH ON FOUR ITEMS.

Reported by a US-federal-government genesis session (docs/feedback/2026-08-15-usgov-genesis-session.md, item 1), independently of the fleet and of a third session the same day. Its own diagnosis is the one worth keeping: 'the point is that the HELPER and the GENERIC path disagree on the field name for the same concept, so reading one does not prepare you for the other.' It also checked the counterweight, which the fleet report did not: Capability takes `description` in both paths, Requirement takes `statement` in both. SO THE INCONSISTENCY IS NOT UNIFORM — it is per-type, which is exactly what makes the mental model survive.

⭐ AND THE SAME DISAGREEMENT HAS A SECOND, FAR MORE EXPENSIVE FORM. `fact:defect-the-constraint-vocabulary-is-documented-as-numeric-so-the-right-node-is-ruled-out` is the helper/prose layer disagreeing with the schema not about a FIELD NAME but about a node type's SCOPE: every description around `Constraint` says 'numeric budget' while the schema requires only name and statement. The same session graded the field-name instance LOW ('costs a full round trip') and the scope instance HIGH ('a modelling-vocabulary gap'). THEY ARE ONE DEFECT AT TWO PRICES. The field-name form announces itself with a validation error and costs a retry; the scope form produces no error at all, and cost that session a wrong conclusion and eleven permanently-open gaps. Fixing only the loud one leaves the expensive one in place.
